newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SIMSMETAL SEES LOWER FINAL DIVIDEND.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SIMSMETAL SEES LOWER FINAL DIVIDEND.

text.p: Metals recycler Simsmetal Ltd said on Tuesday it expected its final dividend to be lower than the previous year because of a 25 percent fall in annual net profit.
"It is likely to be lower than last year because of the lower profit," Simsmetal chief executive John Crabb told a news briefing.
Crabb said the payout ratio would be about the same as the last year.
Earlier Simsmetal released its unaudited 1996/97 results showing a 25 percent fall in net profit to A$35.17 million.
Group profit before interest and tax fell 21 percent to A$$57.64 million on a 19 percent rise in total sales to 4.7 million tonnes.
Fourth quarter net profit rose 64 percent to A$13.109 million and second half earnings were 50 percent higher.
Operating revenues for the year fell marginally to A$1.15 billion, Simsmetal said.
Simsmetal did not declare a final dividend, saying it would announce one in late August.
It declared a final dividend of 21 cents per share, fully franked, in 1995/96.
